chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud said: He informed us that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, said: He narrated to me that Ahmad ibn Isa ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).
Regarding His Exalted Saying, 'Say: These are the appointed times for the people and for the Hajj,' he said: 'For their fasting and their breaking of the fast and their Hajj.'

key_terms.مَوَاقِيتُ: Appointed times or fixed periods for religious rituals

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'appointed times' (mawaqit) refer to in the context of Hajj and fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the 'appointed times' (mawaqit) in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:189 specifically designate the temporal boundaries for the core rituals of fasting, Eid al-Fitr, and Hajj. This exegesis underscores the Shia scholarly view that these divine appointments are not merely chronological markers but sacred periods structuring the spiritual lifecycle of the believer, linking lunar phases directly to acts of worship.
